newsitem.title: TURKEY: Police clash with Islamist marchers after prayers.
newsitem.headline: Police clash with Islamist marchers after prayers.

text.p: Police fired water cannon and used batons to break up a crowd of about 2,000 Islamists protesting in Istanbul against a secularist education bill after Friday noon prayers, witnesses said.
Clashes broke out as police blocked the path of protesters trying to march from a mosque in Istanbul's Cagaloglu district to present a statement to a nearby local education directorate.
At least 10 protesters were arrested and one policeman was injured.

The trouble flared as parliament resumed debate on a draft law to extend compulsory state education to eight years from five. The law would effectively leading to the closure of the first section of religious schools, known as "Imam Hatips".
"Imam Hatips cannot be closed," the protesters chanted as they left the mosque in the historic heart of Istanbul.
The protests have become a weekly event in Istanbul and in towns elsehere in Turkey, prompting tight security outside mosques for Friday prayers, the most important prayers of the week.

The education plans were a central element of demands by the secularist military in Febrary aimed at cracking down on an alleged rise in Islamist activism while the Islam-based Welfare Party was in power.
Turkey's first Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned as prime minister in June under secularist pressure. His government was replaced by a right-left coalition under Mesut Yilmaz.
